land.text: Whydah, 'conquered by King Agaja of the Kingdom of Dahomey' in 1727

successors.note: The page continues the dynasty as a refugee dynasty on offshore islands 'around 1727'; the infobox gives 'Conquest by Dahomey: 1727'; the timeline list ends 'c. 1580-1728'.

capitals.name: Savi (Tanvir)
capitals.note: Infobox capital Savi, also Tanvir; approximate coordinates (the page gives none), placed inland of Ouidah.

correction.text: the coast of Whydah round Savi and Ouidah, 'about 16 km' of coastline in 1700

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Timeline 'Kingdom of Whydah c. 1580-1728'; 'became independent in the late 17th century'; the lead gives the coastline as about 16 km in 1700 and no area. A 40 km circle round Ouidah stands for it (the same circle as the Dahomey and Akwamu dossiers).

region.text: Savi and the coast round Ouidah

ledger.note: c. 1580: the Kingdom of Whydah begins (timeline 'c. 1580-1728'); the infobox says 'Established: 17th century' and the origins section that it 'became independent in the late 17th century'; King Agbangla, the third king, is attested in the 1680s. The page does not say from whom it became independent.

1702 (May): Akwamu seizes Whydah and makes it tributary. 'Little Popo was captured in April, followed by the seizure of Whydah in May'; 'it remained tributary to Akwamu for over two decades' (Akwamu page). Reviewer af-04-x (2026-10-19): added as the mirror of akwamu 1702 vassal_start.
1727 (26 February): Dahomey attacks Whydah. 'On February 26, 1727, Agaja attacked Whydah and burned the palace.'

1727 (February): the Akwamu tie ends with Dahomey's conquest ('Though Whydah was eventually destroyed by Dahomey in the 1720s, it remained tributary to Akwamu for over two decades', Akwamu page). Reviewer af-04-x (2026-10-19): added as the mirror of akwamu 1727 vassal_end.
1727: the fighting ends in Dahomey's conquest. 'In 1727, Whydah was conquered by King Agaja of the Kingdom of Dahomey.'
1727: Whydah is conquered. 'In 1727, Whydah was conquered by King Agaja of the Kingdom of Dahomey.'
1727: the Kingdom of Whydah ends on the mainland; 'The state formed a refugee dynasty on offshore islands after the Dahomeyan invasion around 1727.'

wars.name: Dahomean conquest of Whydah
wars.outcome: Dahomey won: Whydah conquered in 1727; the exiled dynasty's attempts to return ended by 1734 (Agaja page).
wars.note: The Whydah page spells the king Haffon and says nothing of 1733-34; the Agaja page has Huffon's death in July 1733 and the last Whydah faction beaten in 1734.

sources.title: Kingdom of Whydah
sources.note: Infobox (established 17th century, conquest by Dahomey 1727), capital Savi, independent in the late 17th century, King Haffon 1708, timeline c. 1580-1728; no area.

sources.title: Akwamu
sources.note: Akwamu seizure of Whydah in May 1702 and tribute for over two decades (added by reviewer af-04-x).

notes: The Kingdom of Whydah has no Cliopatria row. Two pages opened; the Whydah page is silent on Allada, on any Akwamu conquest or tribute (the Akwamu page, in the Akwamu dossier, has Whydah seized in May 1702 and tributary for over two decades), on the forts' dates, and on the exile after 1727. The capital dot is approximate. King Haffon's rise in 1708 (European trade companies established at Whydah) is the page's only dated event between the 1680s and 1727 and moves no border.
